samples.xml_description:
<module id="serial2parallel">
    <description>Serial-Parallel Conversion Circuit</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal (active low).</input>
        <input id="din_serial">Serial input data.</input>
        <input id="din_valid">Validity signal for input data.</input>
        <output id="dout_parallel" width_description="[7:0]">Parallel output data (8 bits wide).</output>
        <output id="dout_valid">Validity signal for the output data.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="COUNTER_WIDTH">4</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="cnt" width_description="[COUNTER_WIDTH-1:0]">Counter to keep track of the number of serial input data bits received.</reg>
        <reg id="valid" width_description="[0:0]">Valid signal to indicate whether the parallel output data is valid.</reg>
        <reg id="dout_parallel" width_description="[7:0]">Parallel output data register.</reg>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Sequential logic block triggered on the positive edge of clk
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            // Asynchronous reset
            if (!rst_n) begin
                cnt <= 0;
                valid <= 0;
                dout_parallel <= 0;
            end else begin
                // Check if din_valid is asserted
                if (din_valid) begin
                    // Shift the received serial data into dout_parallel
                    dout_parallel[cnt] <= din_serial;
                    
                    // Increment the counter
                    cnt <= cnt + 1;
                    
                    // Check if all 8 bits have been received
                    if (cnt == 7) begin
                        // Set valid to 1 to indicate that dout_parallel contains valid data
                        valid <= 1;
                        
                        // Reset the counter to 0 for the next operation
                        cnt <= 0;
                    end
                end else begin
                    // If din_valid is not asserted, set valid to 0
                    valid <= 0;
                end
            end
        end
    </implementation>
</module>
